decision.evidence: The cited existence/independent-support lemma did not assert optimality of an arbitrary accepted KKT point. Repaired step 1.2 by direct stationarity/complementarity and exact quadratic expansion: for feasible y, the gradient pairing is nonnegative and the positive-definite quadratic remainder is strictly positive away from the candidate. Reviewed equality reduction, exhaustive support completeness, nonsingular solves and finite 2^m enumeration, proving both directions of the infeasible status.

target.evidence: [F1] says feasibility gives a unique minimizer “with a KKT certificate” on an independent support. Step 1.2 applies that existence result to an arbitrary accepted candidate and says [F1] identifies the candidate with the minimizer. Existence of one KKT certificate does not establish that every feasible KKT candidate is optimal; the proof needs universal KKT sufficiency or a direct convexity argument.
